vectors.reason: ENISA names no origin; cloud compute infrastructure and the Annex C ground IT assets (document and configuration management, email servers, OS) sit in ground systems, so a foothold there is the best-supported origin.

review_response.finding: 8 EX-0012 children D-UNDESCRIBED with reason 'the parent covers it'
review_response.action: fixed: policy = a value class that is register, table or data stays K-ACTION (EX-0012.02/.04/.06/.10/.12/.13); subsystem-parameter classes EX-0012.07/.08/.09 dropped with a reason that says why (parameters, not ENISA's data wording).

review_response.finding: IA-0007 enables EX-0012 but IA-0007.02 enables only EX-0012.01; EX-0003 unreachable
review_response.action: fixed: both entries now enable EX-0012, its kept children and EX-0003 (enables list).

review_response.finding: Vector reason cites wording that is not in the description
review_response.action: fixed: vector reason now says Annex C affected assets for the ground IT items.

review_response.finding: Ground-IT half of the threat has no SPARTA fit
review_response.action: kept: SPARTA has no technique that modifies documents, email servers or laptops; the mapping covers registers, authentication, tables and ML data only (see scope_note).

review_response.finding: DE-0003 and EX-0010.01 dropped with 'coded as EX-0012' reason
review_response.action: fixed: reasons rewritten (evasion variant; ransomware's defining outcome is denial).

review_response.finding: m9: nine EX-0012 K-ACTIONs on one sentence; EX-0012.13 on-board while the text names cloud compute
review_response.action: kept, with doubt: .01/.12 follow 'registers', .06 'modification of data', .02/.04/.10 are 'system data' by inference, .13 rests on 'cloud compute infrastructure' and is modelled on board; the ground-IT half is the unmodelled gap in scope_note.

scope_note: IT-side meaning (document/configuration management, email servers, databases, phones/laptops) has no SPARTA technique and is not mapped.

rows.sparta_quote: identity providers, and cloud-hosted mission services
rows.reason: A foothold in ground systems (identity providers, cloud-hosted mission services) is where ENISA's cloud and system data are modified and from where on-board values can be edited.

rows.reason: Writing registers and authentication data on board needs commands sent through the compromised valid ground station.

rows.reason: Parent technique for altering the values and tables a spacecraft decides with; 'registers, system ... processes' in ENISA's definition of the data-modification category.

rows.reason: ENISA names registers explicitly.

rows.enisa_quote: modify registers, system and authentication processes

rows.reason: Routing maps are system data of the 'system processes' ENISA lists; an in-place table edit is data modification.

rows.reason: Subscriber tables are system data of the same kind as routing maps; the edit is data modification.

rows.enisa_quote: modification of data as a threat category
rows.sparta_quote: Payload data, and the metadata that gives it meaning, can be altered in place
rows.reason: Payload data and metadata altered in place is the literal 'modification of data'.

rows.reason: C&DH tables and runtime values are the system data that make up 'system processes'.
